Synopsis:
After the player arrives at Nightsong's prison in the Shadowfell we see Balthazar show up, hot on the player's heels. Balthazar makes his way down towards Nightsong. Variant lines for:1. Met Balthazar in person, agreed to help2. Met Balthazar in person, didn't agree to help 3. Fallback (likely skipped meeting Balthazar)If Balthazar is dead then the player is just shown a cinematic shot of the Shadowfell

Cluster Contexts:
- SHA_Necromancer_Chosen.json: The player meets Balthazar, the necromancer, in his temporary command centre in the Shar temple. They find him at an altar, repairing one of his damaged undead, while other minions bustle around. Balthazar has been sent by Ketheric Thorm to recover Nightsong, but has been unable to clear a path to her vault. He decides to recruit the player, upon recognising them as tadpoled. The player can agree or decline, and can possibly persuade him to loan his flesh golem to aid their exploration.
- SHA_NightsongPrison_NecroAndNightsong.json: If Balthazar is alive when the player reaches Nightsong, they will encounter a dialogue where Balthazar and Nightsong square off. The player has one last chance to betray Balthazar and prevent him from taking Nightsong to Moonrise.
- COL_Necromancer_EnterRoom.json: A player walked into Balthazar's chambers in the colony, while Balthazar is alive, and was spotted by him (or one of his undead). Balthazar reacts with hostility, but players can convince him that they have been turned into thralls.This can only happen if Balthazar is alive at this point and you didn't try the Audience with the Absolute. If you did not send Nightsong to Ketheric, Balthazar would have died in combat in her prison.This dialog will also play when interacting with Balthazar in this route.
- SHA_Necromancer_Barricade.json: The player is challenged by some skeleton warriors at a barricade outside the Necromancer's lair. The necromancer speaks through the dead warriors - his words in their dessicated voices.(this mayor may not follow on from an earlier scene with more skeletons controlled by the necromancer). A mindmeld convinces the necromancer to command his skeletons to grant entry. The scene ends with combat with the skeletons, or a shadowquake triggering a fight between player (+ skeletons) against sharran wraiths. Afterwards, the player is invited into Balthazar's inner sanctum.
- SHA_NightsongPrison_NightsongsFate.json: The player encounter Nightsong, an angelic Aasimar and daughter of Selune who has been trapped in the Shadowfell for a century, first to serve as fodder for Dark Justiciars to kill (they must kill a Selunite to ascend), and then to provide Ketheric with immortality through a soul cage. The player can meet her either alone or with Balthazar. Nightsong is defiant and full of rage. She is immortal, so her current trials are, for her, an annoyance, an indignity, but she knows she will ultimately have her revenge. She regards the player with haughty defiance until she is convinced the player is on her side. If she's freed, she'll have 2 big cinematics of becoming free and cleansed by Selune.

They find him at an altar, repairing one of his damaged undead, while other minions bustle around. Balthazar has been sent by Ketheric Thorm to recover Nightsong, but has been unable to clear a path to her vault. He decides to recruit the player, upon recognising them as tadpoled. The player can agree or decline, and can possibly persuade him to loan his flesh golem to aid their exploration.

context: The player has just arrived at Nightsong’s prison in the Shadowfell, Shar’s domain where Nightsong — a defiant, immortal Selunite — has been held for a century. Balthazar is a necromancer sent by Ketheric Thorm to recover Nightsong; earlier he may have been encountered in the Shar temple where he either recruited the player (recognising them as tadpoled and offering aid such as his flesh golem) or was refused. If Balthazar is alive here he can appear suddenly, arrogant and pleased, and the ensuing lines change depending on whether the player agreed to help, declined, or never met him; the player also has a final chance to betray him at Nightsong’s prison. If Balthazar died earlier in the story (for example during alternate routes), this scene is replaced by a cinematic shot of the Shadowfell. Shadowheart’s comments reflect that this area belongs to Shar and that Balthazar is an intruder.
